mathematical_role: Bounds the expected norm of centered complex Gaussian matrix chaos with a constant independent of the coefficient dimensions.
Specializes the centered estimate to equal dimensions with one logarithmic factor.
Defines the two-by-two nilpotent matrix with one nonzero upper-right entry.
Shows that the example coefficient matrix is non-Hermitian.
Computes the mean and bounds the centered expectation for the nilpotent coefficient.
Computes the mean and bounds the centered norm for rectangular two-by-five coefficients.
The centered integral vanishes when there are no Gaussian coordinates.
Both centered norm integrals vanish when the rectangular coefficients have no rows or no columns.
Computes the balanced moment of one repeated complex Gaussian coordinate at every order.
Evaluates the balanced eighth-order moment of one coordinate as 40320.
Evaluates the zero-order Gaussian product in the empty coordinate space.
Computes the fourth moment as the sum of the two pairings, including repeated labels.
Proves integrability of balanced complex-coordinate monomials with arbitrary repetitions.
Evaluates the fourth moments for one repeated label and for two distinct labels.
Bounds quartic Gaussian tails at cubic-exponential rate with common constants and size cutoff over basis choices.
Specializes the cubic-exponential tail bound to an explicit signed kernel.
Bounds the next Gaussian trace moment by the preceding moment and gives an explicit covariance-norm upper bound for every moment index.
Defines the two coefficient matrices X and Z for a Gaussian matrix series.
Proves that each coefficient in the Pauli example is Hermitian.
Shows that the two specified Pauli coefficients do not commute.
Computes the covariance of the Pauli-coefficient series as twice the identity.
Bounds the fourth operator-norm moment of the Pauli Gaussian series by 24.
Computes the zeroth trace moment and bounds the first trace-moment index by the covariance norm times the dimension.
Computes every trace moment in matrix dimension zero.
Computes the positive even operator-norm moments for an empty coefficient family.
Evaluates the complement coefficients for the specified signed weights and their squares as 3 and 5.
Gives the joint sphere probability estimate for the signed complete phase-unitary example.
Transfers the joint estimate to Haar unitary orbits uniformly over their initial unit vector.
Expresses the sphere operator as a weighted sum of conjugated vector outer products.
Shows that zero weights give a zero centered sphere operator.
Computes both high-weight operators when the number of sites is zero.
Provides exponential high- and low-weight event estimates for the signed example with one linear cutoff.
Counts the low-weight words when there are no sites.
Counts 277 low-weight words for eight sites, four labels, and cutoff fraction one quarter.
Shows that both centered high-weight Gaussian operators vanish for zero shell coefficients.
Computes both centered high-weight Gaussian operators on the empty tensor product.
Computes the mean squared deviation of the normalized Gaussian radius from one as the reciprocal tensor dimension.
Computes the same mean squared deviation for zero sites.
Computes effective order two when the first shell has zero weight.
Computes effective order one for a concrete pair of signed shell weights.
Gives exponential Haar control for the signed Pauli-record example with the full readout operator.
Shows that zero weights give zero linear-cutoff polar compression.
Identifies the low-weight orbit operator with the identity when there are no sites.
Shows that the full second-moment operator, its auxiliary operator, and the associated error vanish at zero coefficients.
Gives a finite net of genuine unitaries for product bases, with cardinality and operator-norm bounds.
Computes the empty tensor product of local unitaries as the identity.
Computes the net cardinality for zero sites.
Bounds the Haar probability of large Gram error for a Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonal unitary family and a fixed initial unit vector.
Computes the Gram error and square sum of an empty orbit family.
Computes the Gram error of a single unitary acting on a unit vector.
Computes the Haar mean squared Gram error of the two-unitary example as two thirds.
Bounds the positive-threshold tail of the Gram error in the two-unitary example.
Computes the positive-threshold Haar tail probability for a singleton unitary family as zero.
